fresh_checks.check: The singular weight selects V_m only; the continuous norm is finite and nondegenerate. The unitary-basis extremal characterization and trace r!N_m/m^r include V_m=0. Metric/weight gauge changes cancel exactly.

For a smooth positive volume the finite-chart submean argument uses a fixed radius for each epsilon and yields the required exp(epsilon m) bound. A general nonpluripolar weighted compact set retains BM as an explicit hypothesis.

P_theta[phi]_I and the compact-obstacle bound control the competitors. Finite maxima, Choquet extraction and pluripolar regularization exceptions produce the largest admissible envelope without an unsupported interchange of supremum and pullback.
Translation, monotonicity, uniform Lipschitz dependence, concavity, multiplier-ideal addition/scaling and the smooth gauge identity preserve the pole conventions.

The extremal bound has no spurious dimension factor. The trace gives a lower supremum bound. Fixed modifications contribute only (n+ord Jac)/m, so Lelong semicontinuity gives all-weight ideal domination. The unconstrained envelope handles thin obstacles before Hartogs upper regularization. No lower-generation conclusion follows.

Differentiating the Gram matrix gives the normalized kernel measure and the negative projection-error Hessian. Equality forces the real continuous variation to be constant by a holomorphic quotient and the identity theorem. Subleading dimension implies vanishing normalized measures and determinants.

Closed-background potential correspondence identifies the competitor families and largest envelopes. Non-pluripolar measures give zero mass to exceptional analytic sets, yielding pushforward, including possibly infinite mass; no arbitrary-measure pullback is used.

The relative-canonical Jacobian factor, multiplier-ideal transformation and volume identity give an isometry and the exact kernel factor, including Jacobian zeros. Intrinsic-degree normalization is retained.

The closed Kähler positive-mass equilibrium theorem is used with its fixed auxiliary line bundle and BM hypotheses. Envelope and measure pushforward give a modification-independent mass. SGPT Theorem 14.3.1 retains its existing external proof scope; it is not independently recertified here.

Integrating weak kernel convergence along tv is justified by bounded normalized dimensions and dominated convergence. Translation and concavity pass to the limit. This does not establish the general Fubini–Study lower bound.

Connected compact fibers give exact section descent. Submersion coordinates and holomorphic local sections identify pullback ideal conditions. Smooth fiber probabilities give a continuous averaging operator and a weakly continuous positive lift. Norm and kernel identities are exact; ambient-degree normalization vanishes when n>q.

The fiber integral of zeta is 2 and the fiber probability is zeta/2. The Hermitian mass identity contributes n, so the limiting lift has factor 1/(2n). Closed pullback curvature has zero ambient top mass, while the Hermitian background admits isolated selecting poles.
Adding an orthonormal complement gives a positive kernel difference with exact total-variation mass q!codim/m^q. Integrating its variation gives the stated determinant bound.

The ambient threshold is max(floor(ma)-n+1,0), while the base threshold is max(floor(ma)-q+1,0). Points in one fiber impose the maximum order. The quotient injects into local jets; surjectivity is unnecessary. The loss is O(m^(q-1)), also for q=1 and fiber dimension zero.

Positive non-pluripolar base mass is explicit. Exact norm descent and the O(1/m) codimension comparison transfer kernel and determinant limits. Small-pole constructions supply sufficient cases without asserting existence for arbitrary coefficients.

Moving poles within one fiber or adding poles with the same maximum coefficient leaves every selected space and kernel unchanged, while large-weight multiplier ideals change at the original point. This is a restricted example, not a closure of the general recovery program.
Gaussian/product and sphere integration give q! product(ell!)/(m+q)!. Selected affine degrees produce the binomial tail, the exact dimension D_m-binom(r_m+q-1,q), and normalized mass 1-a^q.

Chebyshev gives the density limit off t=a; its marginal is q t^(q-1)dt. Entropy bounds by the mode probability yield the potential limit, including t=a, with local uniform convergence away from the pole fiber. The t^m lower bound gives an integrable logarithmic majorant for L1.

All 2107 stored sample points in seven 301-point curves were recomputed from the binomial kernels and limiting potential. Each six-decimal coordinate agrees within 5.01e-7. The potential panel is shifted by one in its stored coordinates and its labels compensate; t<0.01 is omitted as described.

The inner logarithmic potential has rank q-1; the outer potential has curvature sigma. Matching first derivatives give a C1,1 interface without a hypersurface measure. The pole contributes zero non-pluripolar mass.

Analytic ideal domination becomes ordinary logarithmic domination. Complex-line maximum principles identify the envelope. Restriction to the transverse base section and the reverse normal-norm inequality identify the upstairs family. The resulting pole fills the fiber; the raw selecting Hermitian measure can differ on an open set.

For |j|<=C0 m, local Hessian bounds for E^m tensor F^j, holomorphic-frame normalization and radius m^(-1/2) give evaluation norm O(m^d), hence h0=O(m^d). The zero-dimensional case is the finite-point count.

An ambient normal codimension r+1 yields floor(mc)-r, while the base divisor gives floor(mc). Divisibility holds in all tangential variables. Strict positivity of theta-c Theta_Z gives positive base mass. At most r restriction steps, with the uniform linear-twist bound, give O(m^(q-1)); q=1 gives r times the point count.

The common numerator is a sum of squared holomorphic functions, so dd^c phi>=-c(omega_B+omega_F). Choosing b>=c and k>c gives the required Hermitian positivity and base margin. Exact binomial dimensions give the displayed leading loss, with the separate q=1 formula.

The two radial branches are convex in log radius, tangent to the obstacle and match to first order. Exterior complex-line maximum principles impose the divisorial logarithmic bound. Transverse restriction and compactness identify the upstairs family and its enlarged pole set.

The binomial mode has mass at least 1/(d+1). Relative entropy increases above its minimum, yielding Q>=exp(m u_c)/(d+1). Since A_d>=d+1, the full extended-value lower bound holds at every m. A weighted norm changes it by at most -log M/m.

First-tail-term Stirling estimates and geometric ratios apply below R=a; Chebyshev applies above it. Monotonicity plus continuity upgrades to uniform convergence on [delta,1]. The first-success event gives c log R as an L1 lower bound. The marginal q(1-R)^(q-1) yields total mass (k-c)^q.

Norm comparability controls potentials but is insufficient by itself to identify the limiting measure. Concentration of full coherent sections, small projection error on R>a and bounded positive Toeplitz inversion give weighted density w^(-1)B^0+o(A_d). A uniform density bound gives total-variation convergence.

Smooth fiber integration gives a positive smooth base density. Exact kernel descent transfers total variation and the pushforward mass. Intermediate spaces are sandwiched for potentials and differ by O(1/m) normalized mass. Ambient normalization tends to zero.

Testing against products and a countable dense family identifies conditional probabilities almost everywhere on the contact region. A nonconstant positive fiber factor changes the lift and makes the chosen background nonclosed for fiber dimension at least two; in dimension one its derivative vanishes by degree. Moving the center still changes ideals without changing spaces.

Polar integration gives the Gamma monomial norms; angular Parseval and Tonelli give completeness. Bounded jets make the selected space closed. Stirling gives compact convergence of the kernel and all derivatives. Exact full-kernel rescaling sends growing selected orders to zero on fixed scaled compact sets.

The Gamma ratio and bounded second moment yield an O(T^(-1/2)) weighted-Poisson error. The central event uses the derivative of s^(1-alpha); the complement uses Chebyshev and Cauchy–Schwarz. Residue-class thresholds are nonnegative even for q=0, and the error is independent of the order.

For q_m=floor(m lambda), residue thresholds divided by T give zero inside and the curvature density outside R_lambda. Full-kernel bounds control both T>=1 and T<=1 and justify compact-set total variation. The plane measures have infinite total mass, so only local convergence is claimed.

Inside the circle the first selected monomial and a geometric ratio determine the logarithmic branch. Outside the positive density gives the smooth branch. A single degree near m lambda handles the circle itself. The q_m monomial gives an integrable logarithmic lower bound for local L1.

Matching first derivatives produce no circle measure; the logarithmic pole contributes lambda delta_0 to the distributional Laplacian. The maximum principle proves the largest subharmonic competitor. Removing the pole atom gives precisely the non-pluripolar measure.

Uniform central Stirling asymptotics, Riemann sums and Chebyshev tails prove the normal limit with negligible threshold rounding. For arbitrary q_m to infinity, the normalized thresholds tend to -tau and give Phi(tau). The displayed radial expansion distinguishes the selected radius from the full-kernel scale.

The metric remainder is negligible on A R_m precisely in the stated range q_m=o(m^(1/(2r+1))). The upper bound requires local data only. The matching lower bound additionally assumes global semipositivity and strict positivity away from the distinguished point.

Incomplete-Gamma norms agree exponentially with plane norms through k=floor(r c T), by the Gamma exponential moment. Log convexity makes norm ratios increasing and bounds the remaining series geometrically. The first tail is o(S_m). Global restriction gives the upper bound even if the selected space is zero.

The normalized polynomial between q_m and floor(c q_m) captures (Phi(tau)+o(1))S_m. Its omitted model tail is negligible. Gamma moments with the lower metric bound beta|z|^(2r), beta>1/2, control the fixed annulus after choosing A large. The cutoff section has norm at most 1+o(1).

The normalized coefficients grow at most polynomially to a degree O(q_m), with positive lower Gamma bound. On the fixed cutoff annulus phi is positive. Since q_m log m=o(m), the metric weight makes the data exponentially small.

L^m-valued (0,1)-forms are identified isometrically with L^m tensor K_C^(-1)-valued (1,1)-forms. The smoothed logarithm is nonnegative in Hessian near the point and uniformly bounded below in Hessian on its cutoff annulus. A fixed psi handles canonical curvature near the point; strict positivity away absorbs O(q_m+1). The cited Demailly smooth complete-Kähler L2 theorem retains its existing external proof scope.

Weak compactness for each fixed m, fixed-t weighted lower semicontinuity and monotone convergence give |z|^(-2q_m) integrability of the correction. Distributional holomorphy near the point then gives vanishing order at least q_m. Its original norm is exponentially small, so subtraction preserves the selected space.

The shrinking-disc extremal estimate makes the correction negligible at x_m. Phi(tau)>0 and the almost-unit norm give the matching lower limit. The larger-order metric remainder is a limitation of this comparison method; it does not decide the general growing-jets localization problem. Fibration transfer requires the exact descended vanishing conditions.
